decisions.reason: The firm is expanding and has R&D slack, and fouling-detection automation fits its digital monitoring and energy-recovery strategy, so there is no shortfall pressing enough to trigger dropping it.
The weir-dimensioning web tool is cheap to maintain and draws planners toward the firm's core weir hardware, especially now that new weir products D and F have launched.
The fouling-detection system overlaps with A and may eventually be consolidated into it, but growing turnover and available slack let the firm carry it another year.
The spring-controlled flap weir is close to the core flood-control hardware and still early in its life, so results are uncertain but aspirations give no reason to withdraw it.
The energy management system for water facilities matches the firm's strategic direction toward networked, energy-efficient infrastructure, and expansion slack supports continuing it.
The overflow flap gate line has a dedicated page and several models, which signals commitment to a core-adjacent product with low risk of falling short of aspirations.
